subject: Pilot: market-anchored leveling & offer guardrails (US mid-market cohort)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Radford Benchmarks <benchmarks@radford.com>, Tala Talent <sarah@talatalent.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot: market-anchored leveling & offer guardrails (US mid-market cohort)

Team —

I want to propose a small pilot for how we anchor IC leveling and offer guardrails for our US mid-market hires (cloud infra / serving runtime team). Goal: reduce offer variance, shorten negotiation cycles, and test one clear geo multiplier for west-coast vs. rest-of-US.

High level ask:
- Can Talent, Comp, and Finance agree to the proposed anchors below for a 4-person pilot?
- Legal/TA to confirm offer language in the attached template.

Attached: pilot_cohort_offer_template.docx (draft language we currently use).

Proposed quick anchors (week-1 ask — please comment inline):
- IC3: market median (50th) for mid-market benchmarks
- IC4: 70th percentile for direct hire critical skill gaps
- IC5: median + 15% for Sr Eng/Staff targets
- Geo multiplier: 1.08 for Bay Area / NYC; 0.96 for lower-cost metros (trial window: 3 months)

Why pilot? We have three pending offers with StartupX candidates where our current bands are causing long back-and-forth (see Kevin Li, cc'd). If we can validate that these anchors reduce negotiation depth, we can roll to a cohort.

Timeline: please review and reply by EOD May 30. If we get alignment, I'll request headcount confirmation (ENG-67) and loop Legal for final offer language.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Head of Talent & People Ops
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: pilot_cohort_offer_template.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Radford Benchmarks <benchmarks@radford.com>, Tala Talent <sarah@talatalent.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot: market-anchored leveling & offer guardrails (US mid-market cohort)

Thanks Neha — I pulled Radford mid-market slices and attached a short workbook: Radford_Mid-Market_2027.xlsx. I also attached a 2-page summary (comp_bands_proposal_summary.pdf) with recommended anchors.

Quick takeaways: 
- The percentiles you suggested are reasonable; small tweaks below based on role velocity and competitive pressure:
  * IC3: 55th median (we're seeing high competition at 50th for infra SDEs)
  * IC4: 72nd (round to 72 for consistency with Radford cohorts)
  * IC5: 85th for Staff/Principal when hiring for immediate technical lead impact
- Geo multiplier: agree on 1.08 Bay Area / NYC; propose 1.03 for Seattle and remote west coast (we've been underpaying Seattle relative to Bay).
- Sign-on bonus guardrails: 0-15% for IC3/IC4, up to 25% for IC5 with VP approval.

Operational asks / risks:
- We should lock offer ceilings (hard max) for the pilot — see the spreadsheet column "Ceiling_Proposal". If we don't, Finance will flag variability during budget refresh.
- For remote candidates in high-cost metros, require hiring manager justification for >10% over anchor.

Next steps I recommend (short):
1) Agree anchors and ceilings by May 30 (this thread).
2) Neha to file headcount request (ENG-67) and notify Finance.
3) Legal to review offer template and sign-on language (cc'd below).

Cc'd: benchmarks@radford.com — if the numbers look off to you please flag the workbook.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Total Rewards
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Radford_Mid-Market_2027.xlsx, comp_bands_proposal_summary.pdf

On Sat, May 29, 2027 at 11:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Quick takeaways:
> - The percentiles you suggested are reasonable; small tweaks below...

Thanks — concise and helpful. A couple of operational tweaks from my side (comp + TA ops):

- Approval matrix: for this pilot we should require 
  * Hiring Manager + TA for offers at or below anchor.
  * TA + Dir of Eng (or above) for offers 10%+ above anchor.
  * VP approval for anything >20% above anchor or with sign-on >20%.
- Offer language: Legal should confirm we don't expose percentile/benchmarks in the template; keep it internal. Neha, please ensure pilot template redacts any benchmark numbers in candidate-facing copy.
- Headcount: I've started ENG-67 (see link). We can request 2 hires on the pilot budget immediately; additional hires require Finance confirmation.

Please also include a tracker sheet so TA can document candidate-level exceptions (reason, approvals, final comp). If we run the pilot for 3 months we can measure time-to-accept and variance.

I'll approve the two headcount slots once Finance signs off — looping them in next.

—Lauren

Subject: Re: Pilot: market-anchored leveling & offer guardrails (US mid-market cohort)

Agreed. I'm authorizing a limited pilot: 2 hires (engineering infra) using the anchors outlined in Marissa's workbook with the following conditions:
- Approvals: up to 10% above anchor requires Dir+ sign-off; up to 20% requires VP sign-off; anything above 20% requires exec approval.
- Sign-on: up to 15% standard; exceptions need VP approval.
- Finance to confirm budget for two slots (Finance Ops cc'd).

Neha — please proceed to file ENG-67 and get Legal to review the attached offer template. CC me on the final offer letters for the two pilot candidates.

Thanks — and let's measure time-to-accept and offer variance over a 90-day window. If results look good, we'll extend to other teams.
